title: Invertibility of the specified finite comparison
statement: Fix universes $d,t,u$, a prime $\ell$, a field $E$ finite-dimensional over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $Y$ in universe $t$, a finite-field datum $D$ of characteristic $p$ in universe $d$, and $\ell\ne p$. On the small pro-etale site of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ and $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1})_Y$ be the coefficient sheaves [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(B)$ and $D(B_n)$ of module sheaves at coefficient universe $\max(u,t+1)$. Write $H_B,H_{B_n}$ for the recorded derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $F_n:D(B)\to D(B_n)$ for derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and $Q$ for complex localization. For every tensor presentation $a$ of $B$, every $n\ge0$, every reduction presentation $m$ from $a$ at level $n$ [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models], and arbitrary $K,L\in D(B)$, the specified transpose $c_{n,K,L}:F_nH_B(K,L)\to H_{B_n}(F_nK,F_nL)$ is invertible. No completeness or boundedness condition is imposed.

proof.text: The coefficient ring is a DVR and hence Noetherian. The standard quotient resolution and completed-constant-sheaf comparison identify U_n B_n with [B --varpi^(n+1)--> B]. This bounded free complex is K-flat.

proof.text: The scalar adjunction and tensor-Hom adjunction identify restricted finite Hom with H_B(K,U_n N), naturally in N. Take a K-flat source P and K-injective target I; tensoring I with the two-term split-free quotient model remains K-injective.

source.place: paragraphs 1-2: finite-free quotient construction and coefficient adjunction

proof.text: The restricted comparison is represented by f tensor z mapping x to (-1)^(degree(z)*degree(x)) f(x) tensor z. The three differential terms have matching signs bp, a+1+bp and a+bp+p. In each total degree only the two coefficient degrees commute with the product over p, so this chain map is invertible for unbounded P. The presentation normalizations identify it with the specified comparison. Conservative scalar restriction reflects its invertibility.
